text:
maria (Frontend): anyone else seeing the console hang when opening 3+ heatmaps in a row? started after the prefetch routing change rolled out last night. page becomes unresponsive for ~6-10s and charts don't render until reload

ben (Eng-Platform): saw a couple reports in #help earlier. can you paste a HAR or repro steps? which region/canary?

maria (Frontend): eu region, repro in chrome. steps: open dashboard -> click heatmap A -> click heatmap B -> click heatmap C quickly. sometimes the worker pool spikes, then main thread blocks. attaching a tiny repro snippet:

```
// quick repro script
for (let i=0;i<3;i++) fetch(`/api/heatmap?tile=${i}`)
```

ow: logs show lots of prefetch requests routed to the same node, kv cache misses, then console telemetry fanout spikes.

deploy-bot: deploy #prod/2026-03-17 02:14:21 completed to eu-west-1 by ben.

owen (SRE): i captured a flamegraph — main thread time dominated by render + telemetry serialize. also noticed we had many concurrent chunk downloads (~12) and then some 429s from the routing proxy. maybe routing policy affinity is pushing too many prefetches at once.

ben (Eng-Platform): that matches my initial hunch: the routing policy change switched from per-route round robin to affinity-weighted for low-latency, but it didn't cap concurrent prefetches. quota scheduler treats prefetch like high priority now.

natalie (Telemetry): also worth noting telemetry client batches were set to flush on 50ms or 100 events. with the fanout increase we're hitting flush-overhead frequently which blocks. lowering flush frequency helped in local.

maria (Frontend): i tried disabling prefetch in local and it's smooth. with prefetch enabled it's jittery.

ben (Eng-Platform): can you paste the prefetch config? looking for concurrency and throttle values.

maria (Frontend): here's current config from canary:

```
{
  "prefetch": {"enabled": true, "strategy": "affinity", "maxConcurrent": 16, "burst": 8}
}
```

ben (Eng-Platform): aha. maxConcurrent=16 seems high for endpoints that also dump telemetry to client. i'd expect 4-6. i'm going to try a quick canary rollback to the previous routing policy and lower maxConcurrent to 6.

owen (SRE): also add a short-term throttle on telemetry flush: set batchTimeout to 250ms and maxEvents 200. that will reduce the number of small serializing runs.

natalie (Telemetry): agree. i'll push a patch to telemetry client to expose environment flag for batch tuning. we should also start capturing sampling traces by route id so we can see which routes cause the big fanout.

ben (Eng-Platform): plan: 1) revert routing-policy canary -> roll back in eu 2) change prefetch maxConcurrent to 6 and burst to 4 3) telemetry batchTimeout -> 250ms on canary 4) monitor for 2 hours, then escalate to rollback if regression persists.

maria (Frontend): sounds good. i'll create a small smoke test that opens 3 heatmaps quickly and run it in canary after the change.

deploy-bot: rollout started: revert-routing-policy -> eu-west-1 (step 1/3)

ben (Eng-Platform): logging action items: INF-1234 created for followup (prefetch telemetry instrument + routing policy thresholds). i'll watch dashboards.

maria (Frontend): thanks. if it helps, logs i collected:

```
main-thread: task 614ms render
worker-pool: active 12
routing-proxy: 503 spikes then 429s
telemetry-client: flushed 18 times in 2s (avg 110ms)
```

owen (SRE): copying those into the incident timeline. ping me if you want a temporary client-side guard (disable prefetch via query param) while we roll.

ben (Eng-Platform): ok rolling back now, will post updates in 10m. :thumbsup:

maria (Frontend): nice one, thanks all.

(10 minutes later)

ben (Eng-Platform): revert complete, eu looks much better in preliminary smoke. main-thread stalls gone in my quick run. leaving telemetry at higher sample for 30m to be sure.

maria (Frontend): confirmed on my end too. flaky machines still show occasional 1-2s hiccups but no 6-10s freezes. opening INF-1234 with repro + logs.

natalie (Telemetry): i'll follow up with a small RFC for prefetch-aware telemetry tuning so future routing changes don't regress this.

ben (Eng-Platform): thanks team. we'll schedule a deeper postmortem if any further regressions surface.
